provenance: Original content written for this project, with AI assistance (Claude). Item wording, cue-card bullets and follow-up probes are newly authored, not copied or closely adapted from any source. No text is reproduced from Cambridge, IDP, British Council or any other published exam material; only the public format of the test (part structure and timings) is reflected. See GAP-002.

items.prompt: Let's start with where you're from. Tell me about the place you grew up in.
followUpSeeds: What do you like most about living there?
Has it changed much since you were a child?
Would you recommend it to someone visiting for the first time?

items.prompt: Now I'd like to ask about what you do each day. Do you work, or are you studying?
followUpSeeds: What's the most demanding part of that?
How did you come to choose it?
Is it something you can see yourself doing in ten years?

items.prompt: Let's talk about technology. Which device do you use most on an ordinary day?
followUpSeeds: What would change if you had to manage without it for a week?
Do you use it more than you'd like to?
How do you think people handled this before it existed?

items.prompt: Is there a part of your town or city that you always go back to? Tell me about it.
followUpSeeds: What is it about that place that keeps you returning?
Who do you usually go there with?
Has it changed since you first started going?

items.prompt: What do you usually do in the first hour of your working or studying day?
followUpSeeds: Is that a routine you chose or one that just developed?
What would an ideal start to the day look like for you?
Do you ever skip it when you are short of time?

items.prompt: Tell me about the last time a piece of technology frustrated you.
followUpSeeds: How did you eventually deal with it?
Do you tend to fix problems yourself or ask someone?
Does that kind of frustration make you want to use less technology?

items.prompt: Let's talk about getting around. How do you usually travel on an ordinary weekday?
followUpSeeds: Would you change anything about that if you could?
How long does it take, and does it feel too long?
How is it different at weekends?

items.prompt: When you go away for a few days, do you plan everything in advance or leave things open?
followUpSeeds: Has leaving things open ever gone wrong for you?
Who in your family is the planner?
What is the one thing you always book first?

items.prompt: Let's talk about learning. What is something you have taught yourself recently?
followUpSeeds: What made you want to learn it?
Where did you find the help you needed?
What was the hardest moment along the way?

items.prompt: Do you learn better on your own or together with other people?
followUpSeeds: Can you give an example of a time when working with others helped?
Is there anything you can only learn alone?
Has your answer changed since you were younger?

items.prompt: Let's talk about food. What did you have for breakfast today, and is that typical for you?
followUpSeeds: Do you think breakfast is an important meal?
Is there a food you eat at breakfast that you would not eat at other times?
How did your family eat in the mornings when you were young?

items.prompt: Do you enjoy cooking, or would you rather have someone else do it?
followUpSeeds: What is the one dish you are confident making?
Who taught you to cook, if anyone?
Do you cook differently when you are cooking for guests?

items.prompt: Let's talk about looking after yourself. How do you usually unwind after a tiring day?
followUpSeeds: Does that really help you recover?
Is it something you do alone or with others?
What do you do when you have no energy at all?

items.prompt: Have you ever tried to change a habit that was bad for you?
followUpSeeds: What made you decide it was time?
What helped you most, or got in the way?
What advice would you give someone trying the same thing?

items.prompt: Let's talk about your surroundings. How much green space is there near where you live?
followUpSeeds: How often do you actually use it?
Would you like there to be more?
How do people in your area generally treat it?

items.prompt: What, if anything, do you do at home to cut down on waste?
followUpSeeds: Is it easy to keep up, or does it take effort?
Do the people you live with do the same?
What is one thing you know you could do better?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a piece of work you were proud of. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: and explain why you were proud of it
followUpSeeds: Would you approach it differently if you started again today?
Did anyone else understand how much effort it took?
What did it teach you that you still use?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a journey that did not go as planned. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: and explain how you felt about it afterwards
followUpSeeds: Looking back, was anything about it worth the trouble?
Could it have been avoided?
Has it changed how you prepare for trips now?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe someone who taught you something useful. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: and explain why it stayed with you
followUpSeeds: Have you ever passed that on to someone else?
Would the same approach work for everyone?
What made them different from other people who tried to teach you?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a place where you do your best work or thinking. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: what it looks and sounds like
and explain why it suits you so well
followUpSeeds: Would you be as productive somewhere else?
Have you ever tried to recreate that atmosphere elsewhere?
Does anyone else share that space with you?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a day trip to a place you had not planned to visit. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: what you did while you were there
and explain whether you would return
followUpSeeds: Would you go back there on purpose?
Do you think surprises like that are better than planned outings?
Did you tell other people about it afterwards?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a skill you are trying to get better at. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: and explain what level you hope to reach
followUpSeeds: How do you know whether you are actually improving?
What would stop you from continuing?
Is there anyone you compare yourself with?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a building in your hometown that you know well. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: what the building is and where it stands
and explain why it matters to you
followUpSeeds: Would visitors find it as interesting as you do?
Has its purpose changed over the years?
What would the area lose if it disappeared?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a local event or tradition from the place you grew up. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: and explain what it means to the community
followUpSeeds: Do younger people still take part in the same way?
Would it make sense to someone from outside the area?
Has it become more or less commercial over time?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe an app or gadget that made an everyday chore easier. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: and explain whether you would recommend it
followUpSeeds: Did it also create any new problems?
How did you do the same job before you had it?
Would you still use it if it became expensive?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a time when technology failed you at a bad moment. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: and explain how the situation ended
followUpSeeds: What did that teach you about depending on it?
Did you have a back-up plan?
How did the other people involved react?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a meal you cooked or helped prepare for other people. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
followUpSeeds: Would you cook the same thing again for the same people?
What was the most stressful part of the preparation?
Did anyone offer to help, and did you let them?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a dish from your family that you hope to pass on. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: and explain why you want to keep it alive
followUpSeeds: Who in the family makes it best?
Does it change from one generation to the next?
Could someone outside the family make it just as well?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a form of exercise you tried and either kept up or gave up. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: how you came to try it
what you liked or disliked about it
and explain why you kept it up or stopped
followUpSeeds: Would you ever go back to it?
What would have made it easier to continue?
Did anyone encourage or discourage you?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a time when you really needed rest and had to force yourself to take it. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: how you realised you needed a break
and explain what you learned from it
followUpSeeds: What finally made you stop?
How did you feel afterwards?
Do you now notice the warning signs sooner?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a natural place near you that you would want to see protected. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: and explain why it deserves protection
followUpSeeds: Who do you think is responsible for looking after it?
Have you seen it threatened in any way?
What would you say to someone who wanted to build there?

items.prompt: I'd like you to describe a change you made in your life to be kinder to the environment. You have one minute to prepare, and then I'd like you to speak for two minutes.
bullets: and explain whether it was worth the effort
followUpSeeds: Was the change as hard as you expected?
Did other people notice or copy you?
What is the next change you might make?

items.prompt: Let's consider work more generally. Do you think people expect more from their jobs than they used to?
followUpSeeds: What do you think is driving that change?
Is that expectation a realistic one?
How might it look a generation from now?

items.prompt: Let's think about travel more broadly. Some people argue that cheap flights have made travel less meaningful. What's your view?
followUpSeeds: Who benefits most from that change?
Could it be managed differently?
Is there a cost that doesn't show up in the ticket price?

items.prompt: Let's talk about careers. Is it better for a society when people stay in one line of work, or when they change often?
followUpSeeds: Does the answer depend on the type of job?
How should schools prepare people for that?
Who is most affected when careers keep shifting?

items.prompt: Let's consider travel and transport. Do you think people still value the journey itself, or only where they end up?
followUpSeeds: Has faster travel changed what people expect?
Are there journeys that are better slow?
How might that attitude differ between generations?

items.prompt: How do you think transport in big cities will change over the next few decades?
followUpSeeds: Who is likely to gain or lose from those changes?
What stands in the way of improving public transport?
Would you personally welcome those changes?

items.prompt: Let's discuss education. Is formal schooling still the best way to gain useful skills?
followUpSeeds: What can people learn better outside the classroom?
Who should pay for ongoing learning in adult life?
How is the role of schools likely to change?

items.prompt: What qualities make someone good at teaching, as opposed to simply knowing a subject?
followUpSeeds: Can those qualities be trained, or are they natural?
How much does a teacher's personality matter?
Do you think technology can replace some of those qualities?

items.prompt: Let's discuss where people live. Why do so many young people leave small towns for big cities?
followUpSeeds: What do small towns lose when that happens?
What could small towns do to keep young people?
Do you think the trend will continue?

items.prompt: How important is it for a place to protect its old buildings and customs?
followUpSeeds: Who should pay to keep them going?
When does protecting the past start to hold a place back?
Which things from your own area would you most want to protect?

items.prompt: Do you think people rely on technology too much for things they could do themselves?
followUpSeeds: Which skills are most at risk of being lost?
Does it matter if those skills fade?
How could people keep a healthy balance?

items.prompt: How has technology changed the way people make and keep friendships?
followUpSeeds: Are online friendships as meaningful as face-to-face ones?
Who is most affected by this, young or old?
What might be lost as more contact moves online?

items.prompt: Do you think people eat more healthily today than in the past?
followUpSeeds: What has made healthy food easier or harder to find?
How much do advertising and price affect what people buy?
How might eating habits look in thirty years?

items.prompt: Should governments try to influence what people eat?
followUpSeeds: What kind of measures would be acceptable?
Where does personal choice end and public responsibility begin?
Have you seen any such policy work well?

items.prompt: Whose responsibility is it to keep a population healthy: individuals, employers or governments?
followUpSeeds: How can employers support health without being intrusive?
Is it fair to expect the same of rich and poor?
What would you prioritise if you had a limited budget?

items.prompt: Why do many people find it so hard to rest properly in modern life?
followUpSeeds: How much of this is due to work culture?
What role does technology play?
What could society do to make rest easier?

items.prompt: Who should carry the main cost of protecting the environment: individuals, companies or governments?
followUpSeeds: What happens when each group waits for the others to act?
Is it fair that poorer countries are asked to make the same sacrifices?
What do you think is the most effective single measure?

items.prompt: Do you think individual choices make a real difference to environmental problems?
followUpSeeds: Why do many people feel their actions do not matter?
Can small habits spread and add up?
Which matters more, personal habits or large-scale policy?
